grade4-programme-packet.kind: Original French connected text and production tasks, additional to the complete earlier claim checks

fiction.title: Une place pour les histoires
fiction.body: Nora et Sami préparent un coin lecture pour leur classe. Ils trouvent une boîte de livres près de la fenêtre. Nora propose de lire tous ensemble. Sami préfère aussi garder une place pour lire seul. Ils dessinent deux petits espaces sur leur plan. Une camarade demande : « Où pouvons-nous poser nos dessins ? » Nora ajoute une table près des livres. Le groupe regarde le nouveau plan et explique ses choix.
fiction.visualPreparation: Prepare actual original panels showing the found book box, the two proposed activity spaces and the final drawing table. One visible detail, such as a blue notebook under the table, is compatible but not stated in the text. Retain prediction/confirmation, words-to-picture and illustration-only detail checks. For mental visualisation use an unillustrated scene first, then a changed image and reconsider a supported inference.

writingModels.information: Notre coin lecture propose deux activités. On peut lire seul ou partager une histoire avec le groupe. Les dessins sont sur la table près des livres. Les deux espaces permettent de choisir comment participer.
writingModels.request:
Bonjour Madame Ali,
Nous préparons le coin lecture. Pouvez-vous nous aider à trouver une boîte et des feuilles ? Nous souhaitons présenter notre plan à la classe.
Merci,
Nora et Sami
writingModels.instructions: Choisis un livre. Pose ton dessin sur la table. Explique ton idée à un camarade. À la fin, range le livre dans la boîte.

grade4-programme-packet.task: Read/understand the actual connected French story and a supplied information or media piece, using appropriate before/during/after strategies. Identify actual ideas/details, retell and compare purpose/structure/features. Produce a fresh structured information note, an audience-specific request and an ordered instruction piece, plus a narrative alternative; select form/reader/purpose, plan, draft, revise content/order after feedback, edit actual conventions and publish/share. The models are supports, not copied learner outcomes. Retain all earlier whole-claim tasks, authentic sources, four writing modes and channel-specific reflection.

early-immersion-packet.kind: Original supported early-primary French task collection; fictional contexts are available
early-immersion-packet.newReadingMessage:
Bonjour Zoé,
Je cherche un livre pour notre rencontre. Dans la classe, les livres sont dans la boîte bleue. Mon ami Sami choisit une histoire avec un chat. Peux-tu choisir une autre histoire ? Nous pouvons les raconter ensemble.
À bientôt,
Nora

writingModels.invitation:
Bonjour Zoé,
Viens découvrir une histoire dans notre coin lecture. Tu peux choisir un livre de la classe. Quelle histoire préfères-tu ?
À bientôt,
Nora
writingModels.information: Voici notre coin lecture. Les livres sont dans la boîte. Les dessins sont sur la table. On peut lire ou écouter une histoire.
writingModels.narrative: Nora cherche son livre. Sami regarde sous la table et trouve le livre bleu. Nora remercie son ami. Ils lisent ensemble.

early-immersion-packet.task: Use the earlier complete oral set across self, supplied fictional family, friends and classroom, not only one greeting. Teach familiar meanings with a qualified French model and accurate contextual/visual/auditory support. Read the actual message and matched familiar connected story; interpret its meaning and features rather than copy a response. Plan and create fresh brief French messages for varied readers/purposes using actual models, shared/guided/independent work and content revision. A learner may choose a supplied fictional persona; no family disclosure is required. The source’s early supports remain available; no automatic requirement to perform a later unscripted academic debate is imported.

beyond-independent-readaloud.kind: Original French read-aloud support plus an actual learner-relative selection condition
beyond-independent-readaloud.text: Dans notre histoire, deux groupes préparent une rencontre de lecture. Le premier souhaite raconter une aventure à toute la classe, tandis que le second propose plusieurs petits groupes. Chaque groupe explique ce qui l’aiderait à participer. Nora remarque que les deux propositions peuvent avoir une place dans le même projet. Elle demande quels livres et quels espaces sont disponibles avant de choisir un plan. Les camarades changent leur proposition après avoir écouté les idées des autres. Le projet ne ressemble plus au premier dessin, mais chacun peut expliquer ce qui a changé et pourquoi.
beyond-independent-readaloud.selection: Use actual French fiction, information AND the original verse from the prior oral packet. Before use verify which text is beyond this learner’s independent French reading while remaining accessible through supported listening. This text is a candidate, not proof of that relation; if already independently readable, prepare and check another age-appropriate text. Do not assert a nominal grade, a difficult word or reading aloud alone establishes beyond-independent selection.
beyond-independent-readaloud.task: Hear actual French, ask/answer questions about key details, discuss characters/events or ideas and request clarification when needed. The reading-level relation is checked separately from listening meaning; an English translation or the already independently decoded story alone is insufficient.

spontaneous-exchange.kind: Actual open-response task with supportive French stems, not a complete prescribed dialogue
contexts: Choose a familiar class book/game or discuss a fictional character’s preference.
For later courses, discuss the actual reading-corner project or supplied twelve-book/two-space academic proposal.
spontaneous-exchange.task: Begin with a planned/rehearsed report or exchange. A peer gives an actual unrehearsed relevant view, clarification request or changed available resource; the learner listens, asks/answers, builds on it and adapts the message. A teacher separately asks an open relevant question and responds to the learner’s actual answer. In increasingly spontaneous profiles require smooth intelligible familiar French follow-up beyond reciting the rehearsed report; self-repair and permitted modelling/support remain. In early/Extended structured-guided profiles retain the stated task framework while replies remain real. Do not substitute a fully memorised complete exchange.

word-strategies.kind: Several actual French word-learning resources with fresh use
word-strategies.task: Preview familiar/unknown words, use actual context/picture clues, ask a meaning question, confirm with a checked reference and connect with a known word; record a useful entry in a personal French word/picture bank and use it meaningfully in a changed reading/writing/speaking context. Later profiles use several different strategies and show why one helps in the actual case; early profiles use the source-supported few methods. No universal strategy-count tier or Greek/Latin-root inventory is inferred. Actual new targets and prepared references must be checked rather than merely named.

process-and-reflection.kind: Complete source-specific process and reflection duties across actual tasks
process-and-reflection.writing: Across the portfolio use actual modelled, shared, guided and independent writing episodes; say or note ideas before drafting, gather several resources, use a story beginning/middle/end plan and a suitable organiser for information. For later course D2 criteria, establish task success criteria before drafting and actually inspect content, clarity and interest against them; a final template alone is insufficient. Use actual print AND electronic/other resources as appropriate, teacher/peer content feedback, a reasoned revision, familiar French spelling/accents, punctuation, grammar/intended-time checks and presentation choices. Share a finished piece by reading the learner’s own French writing to peers/teacher and use a digital tool to type/publish actual words. Retain whole sentence, process-vocabulary, feedback and sustained-writing readiness; do not create unrelated tasks solely to certify a prerequisite.
process-and-reflection.reflection: Keep listening, speaking, reading and writing reflection distinct: discuss before/during/after strategies with both teacher and peers, identify an actual supported strength/less-secure operation, set a concrete small goal and monitor it in a later task. Discuss listening barriers in the profiles where required; plausible examples may be considered without inventing a learner failure or forcing distress. An old English goal or a reflection only about another channel does not certify the French operation.
process-and-reflection.limits: Examples of every tense, gender ending, suffix, presentation device or text product are not mandatory inventories. Prepare language/complexity suited to actual source duties; the report is an authoring design, not a learner performance receipt.

actions: Retain every exact bound earlier whole protocol and its actual French corpus/resources, not only its title. Use the complete original oral set across self, fictional family, friends and environment, with supplied academic/personal subject matter where required. Listening checks purpose, main ideas/details, meaning strategies and actual context/visual cues, plus the full learner-relative beyond-independent fiction/information/verse listening task.

Complete the introduced French noun/action/feeling recall, the full oral/nasal and consonant/cluster contrast checks using a qualified model of the intended variety, and actual connected phrasing/intonation. A legitimate regional in/un merger is not an error; intelligibility, accurate intended contrasts and meaningful French use are checked distinctly, not inferred from English phonics or an isolated echo.

Give a real organised approximately one-minute report with at least three facts, descriptive details and understandable delivery; review actual recording/live feedback for clarity, pace and relevant details. Recount a different familiar event with beginning/middle/end and select language for a peer versus teacher audience. These retain the existing whole report claim, not an official universal time requirement. Use an accessible listener-engagement strategy and actually respond to another viewpoint; no forced eye contact or affect score.

Use spontaneous-exchange in its declared course structure with actual peer AND teacher replies. Ask a relevant information/clarification question, respond specifically, continue several turns, build on a view with a reason and keep the agreed topic. A fully prescribed dialogue or question-and-answer from a different French corpus cannot stand for the task.

Reading uses actual familiar connected text with meaning and fluency checks, the complete26-word sight bank and word-learning strategies. Preserve actual picture/text prediction/confirmation, wording-to-illustration and compatible illustration-only detail checks, plus unillustrated mental imagery and revision after new evidence. A picture label, isolated word recognition or new-word inference alone is insufficient.

Use an actual collection spanning fiction, information, graphic and media forms: original adaptations alongside the earlier checked authentic French school calendar and library information/media page. Interpret actual purpose, word/style choices, structure and presentation contribution; different form headings alone are insufficient. Both adapted and authentic material are present across the set; no claim is made that the publisher mandates eight separate products.

Writing retains actual audience/form/tone choices and coherent opening/development/closing, several forms and the whole process in process-and-reflection. Follow actual models and source-appropriate criteria, revise content/order after feedback, edit French conventions and prepare/read/type a real finished piece. Separately check taught exact French forms/accents and nontransparent spellings after a delay without a written model, in changed meaningful writing; supported editing alone is not retained orthographic knowledge.

Perform each actual listening/speaking/reading/writing reflection and monitored goal in its own channel, with teacher AND peer discussion. The previous whole reflection/planning/goal operations remain unchanged; generic learning labels and age bands do not establish performance.

Use the actual academic project report/table/poster and word-strategies resources in addition to familiar personal contexts; add original French reading/writing/reporting at the course’s source-comparable complexity. The Core starter story alone does not establish the later academic duties.
nearMiss: Only retags old source codes or ages, copies a full model or imports an English/different-French-corpus result.
Omits the actual source-required spontaneous response, unfamiliar listening word, academic context, word strategy or channel-specific reflection.
Treats a nominal grade or story title as a verified beyond-independent reading relation.
